title: CRLA/345/2018 of RAVI PANDEY Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text: HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL

Criminal Appeal No. 345 of 2018
Ravi Pande and others ..... Appellants

Versus
State of Uttarakhand ....Respondent
Ms. Pushpa Joshi, Sr. Advocate, assisted by Mr. Ganesh Kandpal and Ms. Chetna Latwal,
Advocate for the appellants.
Mr. V.K. Jemini, A.G.A., assisted by Mr. Balwinder Singh, Brief Holder for the State of
Uttarakhand.
Coram: Hon'ble Alok Singh, J.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Ravindra Maithani, J.(Oral)
This appeal is preferred against the judgment and order
dated 01.10.2018 passed in Sessions Trial No.01 of 2018, State Vs. Ravi
Pande and others, under sections 498-A, 304-B and 302 IPC and 3/4
Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, by the court of learned District and
Sessions Judge, Bageshwar.
2. By the impugned judgment and order, the appellants
Ravi Pande, Mahesh Chandra Pande and Tarkeshwari Pande have been
acquitted of the charges under sections 304-B IPC and 3/4 of Dowry
Prohibition Act, 1961, but, they have been convicted of the charges under
sections 302, 498-A IPC and are sentenced as hereunder:-
 "(i) The appellant Ravi Pande is convicted under section
302 IPC and sentenced with life imprisonment and a fine
of Rs.50,000/-. In default of payment of fine, he shall
undergo simple imprisonment for a further period of one
year.

2
 (ii) The appellant Mahesh Chandra Pande is convicted
under section 302 IPC and sentenced with life
imprisonment and a fine of Rs.50,000/-. In default of
payment of fine, he shall undergo simple imprisonment for
a further period of one year.

(iii) The appellant Smt. Tarkeshwari Devi @ Tara Devi is
convicted under section 302 IPC and sentenced with life
imprisonment and a fine of Rs.5000/-. In default of
payment of fine, she shall undergo simple imprisonment
for a further period of six months.
 (iv) The appellant Km. Ruchi Pande is convicted under
section 302 IPC and sentenced with life imprisonment and
a fine of Rs.5000/-. In default of payment of fine, she shall
undergo six months simple imprisonment for a further
period of six months.
 (v) The appellant Ravi Pande is also convicted under
section 498-A IPC and sentenced with three years rigorous
imprisonment and a fine of Rs.25,000/-. In default of
payment of fine, he shall undergo simple imprisonment for
a further period of six months.
(vi) The appellant Mahesh Chandra Pande is also
convicted under section 498-A IPC and sentenced with
three years rigorous imprisonment and a fine of
Rs.25,000/-. In default of payment of fine, he shall
undergo simple imprisonment for a further period of six
months.
 (vii) The appellant Smt. Tarkeshwari Devi @ Tara Devi is
also convicted under section 498-A IPC and sentenced
with three years rigorous imprisonment and a fine of
Rs.5000/-. In default of payment of fine, she shall undergo
simple imprisonment for a further period of one month.
 (viii) The appellant Km. Ruchi Pande is also convicted
under section 498-A IPC and sentenced with three years
rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs.2000/-. In default
of payment of fine, she shall undergo one month's simple
imprisonment for a further period of one month.
The period, already served shall be adjusted. Both the
sentences shall run concurrently"

3
3. Facts, as unfolded by the prosecution, briefly stated as
hereunder:-
(i) On 18.05.2017, deceased Arti was missing from her house. A
search was made and she along with appellant Ravi Pande was located at
Haldwani. Both of them revealed that they were in love and would marry.
Subsequently, appellant Ravi Pande and his family members declined to
marry deceased Arti. Deceased Arti revealed that she was carrying a
child of appellant Ravi Pande in her womb. On 23.06.2017, deceased
Arti lodged an FIR of rape against Ravi Pande. Thereafter, Ravi Pande
and his family members agreed to marry deceased Arti. Appellant Ravi
Pande and deceased Arti married on 05.07.2017 in Arya Samaj Mandir,
Rudrapur and the marriage was registered. Thereafter, appellant Ravi
Pande filed a petition in the High Court for quashing the FIR, which had
been lodged by the deceased Arti against him for the commission of rape.
The FIR was quashed. Appellant Ravi Pande stayed for a while with
deceased Arti and left for his job. He was in Army. Appellant's father is
also a retired Army person.
(ii) On 13.09.2017, PW2 Vimla Devi was informed by his niece
that Arti had consumed poison and she is calling this witness. PW2
Vimla Devi reached in the house of deceased Arti. It was about 10:00 -
10:30 in the morning. She inquired as to what had happened, to which,
deceased Arti replied that none is present in her house. She had gone for
collecting grass. When she returned, she did not find any family members
in the house. She went into the kitchen and drank water from a bucket.
After drinking water, there was immense irritation in her chest. PW2
Vimla Devi took deceased Arti as well as the bucket immediately to the

4
hospital in 108 vehicle. On her way, deceased Arti told to this witness
that her mother-in-law, father-in-law had poisoned the water and left the
house. All family members had conspired with her mother-in-law and
father-in-law. In the hospital, during treatment, she died. Concerned
Revenue Officer visited the hospital. He inquired from PW2 Vimla Devi
and took into custody the bucket with water in it. On 13.09.2017 itself,
inquest of the deceased Arti was prepared and on the same day, post-mortem of the deceased Arti was conducted. Viscera was preserved for
further forensic examination. On 16.09.2017 a report was lodged by PW2
Vimla Devi. Forensic report was also obtained, which detected organo-chloro insecticide in the viscera as well as in the water sample taken from
the bucket. The Investigating Officer prepared a site plan and after
investigation, submitted the chargesheet against the appellants for the
offences punishable under sections 498-A, 304-B and 302 IPC and 3/4
Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961. Cognizance was taken and the case was
committed to the court of sessions for trial.
4. On 07.03.2018, charges under sections 498-A, 304-B and
302 IPC and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 were framed against the
appellants. Appellants denied the charges and claimed trial.
5. The prosecution, in order to establish the case, examined
as many as seventeen witnesses, namely, PW1 CP Naresh Kumar, PW2
Vimla Devi, PW3 Khema Nand Khulbe, PW4 Tara Datt Khulbe, PW5
Tribhuwan Singh Bora, PW6 Neema Khulbe, PW7 Bhagirathi Devi,
PW8 Jivanti Devi, PW9 Dr. Manish Pant, PW10 Himanshu Khulbe,

5
PW11 Dr. Vidit Pande, PW12 Mahesh Chandra Tiwari, PW13 Subhash
Chandra Arya, PW14 Bhagwati Devi, PW15 Mahesh Chandra Joshi,
PW16 C.O. Veer Singh and PW17 Dr. Dayal Sharan.
6. Appellants were examined under Section 313 of the
Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Code').
According to the appellants, they have been falsely implicated. They did
not poison the water. In defence, three witnesses have been examined.
7. After hearing the parties, based on the evidence, the learned
court below vide judgment and order dated 01.10.2018, convicted and
sentenced the appellants. As stated hereinbefore, aggrieved, the instant
appeal.
8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the
record.
9. On behalf of the appellants, it is argued that none of the
appellants were in the house when deceased Arti died. The deceased was
never harassed for dowry. Deceased and appellant Ravi Pande were in
love, before they got married. There is no evidence that appellants mixed
poison in water. FIR is delayed. Learned Senior Counsel would argue
that it is a criminal case. It cannot be decided on the basis of assumptions.
There should be some evidence to bring home the guilt of the appellants.
It is argued that if on 13.09.2017, deceased Arti had revealed that she was

6
poisoned by the appellants by mixing poison in the drinking water, why
FIR was not lodged soon after her death.
10. It is argued that there is no explanation for delay in
lodging FIR. In her statement, DW1 Ruchi Pande has stated that there
was water purifier in the kitchen. It also falsifies the statement of Vimla
Devi because having water purifier in the kitchen, the deceased would
not have taken water from a bucket. Prosecution failed to prove the
charges against the appellants beyond reasonable doubt. Hence, the
appellants deserve to be acquitted of the charges and appeal allowed.
11. On the other hand, learned State Counsel would argue
that this case is proved beyond reasonable doubt against the appellants. It
is argued that it is a case of murder. The conduct of appellants is relevant.
The circumstances under which the deceased was married to appellant
Ravi Pande and thereafter her harassment at the hands of the appellants
for the demand of dowry. According to learned State Counsel, soon
before her death, deceased Arti revealed it to her mother Vimla Devi that
the appellants mixed poison in the drinking water to kill the deceased.
When deceased drank water from it, she felt irritation in her chest.
According to learned State Counsel, this statement is also relevant under
section 6 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 as part of the same
transaction.
12. Learned State Counsel further argued that deceased died
in the house of the appellants. The burden was upon the appellants to tell

7
as to how did the deceased die, under section 106 of the Indian Evidence
Act, 1872. This burden has not been discharged by the appellants.
Therefore, it is argued that prosecution has proved the case beyond
reasonable doubt. Statement of PW2 Vimla Devi is supporting the
statement of other family members. Similarly, the statement of PW6
Neema Khulbe, her daughter corroborates her statement. Not only this,
the forensic report also corroborates and supports the prosecution case.
Therefore, according to prosecution, it has been able to prove the case
beyond reasonable doubt. Hence, the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
13. PW1 Naresh Kumar is a formal witness; he prepared the
chik FIR.
14. PW2 Vimla Devi is the star witness. She is mother of the
deceased Arti. According to her, deceased Arti had done polytechnic
from Haldwani. She was married to appellant Ravi Pande on 05.07.2017.
After marriage, Ravi Pande and deceased Arti stayed together for 12-13
days at Haldwani and thereafter appellant Ravi Pande left for job and
deceased came to her matrimonial house in village Manyura, where she
finally died. PW2 Vimla Devi states that appellant Ravi Pande would
harass the deceased Arti for the demand of dowry and other appellants
would also torture and harass her. On a Monday, before the death of the
deceased Arti, according to PW2 Vimla Devi, deceased had revealed it to
her that appellants scolded her for the demand of dowry and after three
days on Wednesday, she died. On that day, niece of this witness called
her that deceased had consumed poison or she was administered poison.

8
This witness reached there. Deceased revealed it to her that there was
none in her family at that time. She had also gone for collecting grass.
When she returned, she drank water from a bucket in the kitchen and
soon thereafter she started feeling irritation in the chest. She was taken to
the hospital along with bucket. In hospital, she died. Revenue Officer
took into custody the bucket and water in it. This witness has also stated
that before the marriage, Ravi Pande and deceased Arti had eloped from
the village. They were located at Haldwani. Deceased Arti was pregnant
due to her relationship with appellant Ravi Pande. They were married,
but her foetus was got aborted by the appellants. According to PW2
Vimla Devi, in a pre-planned manner, deceased Arti was killed by the
appellants.
15. PW3 Khema Nand Khulbe corroborates the statement of
PW2 Vimla Devi. According to him, he also reached in the house of
deceased, when she was unwell and revealed it to PW2 Vimla Devi that
after drinking water from the bucket, she felt irritation in the chest. This
witness proved the bucket in the court.
16. PW4 Tara Datt Khulbe has stated the circumstances,
under which the appellant Ravi Pande and deceased Arti were married.
According to him, on 17.05.2017, appellant Ravi Pande and deceased
Arti disappeared from the village. They were located in Haldwani when
they revealed that they were in love. It was agreed between the families
of both of them that they would be married, but subsequently, parents of
Ravi Pande declined to it. As the deceased Arti was pregnant, due to her

9
relationship with the appellant Ravi Pande, an FIR was lodged for
commission of rape. Thereafter, appellant Ravi Pande and deceased Arti
were married. FIR was quashed. This witness has also stated that about 2-
3 days prior to her death, deceased Arti revealed it to him that she was
being harassed for the demand of dowry. This witness also reached in the
hospital, where the deceased has been taken.
17. PW5 Tribhuwan Singh Bora is the Revenue Officer, who
reached in the hospital after having received the information that
deceased Arti consumed poison. He prepared the site plan, where the
dead body was laid, prepared inquest and forwarded the dead body for
the post-mortem. According to him, he also took into custody the empty
bucket and the bottle filled with water. He identified those articles in the
court.
18. PW6 Neema Khulbe corroborates the statement of PW2
Vimla Devi, her mother and PW4 Tara Datt Khulbe about relationship of
both the deceased Arti and appellant Ravi Pande and about harassment,
which according to her, deceased met with.
19. PW7 Bhagirathi Devi has been declared hostile by the
prosecution. According to her, on 13.09.2017, at 10:00 in the morning,
the deceased requested her to call her mother saying that she was not
feeling well.
20. PW8 Jivanti Devi has also been declared hostile.

10
21. PW9 Dr. Manish Pant conducted the post-mortem of the
deceased. According to him, cause of the death could not be ascertained,
therefore, viscera was kept for examination. He also explained about the
condition of the other body organs.
22. PW10 Himanshu Khulbe, brother of the deceased has
stated that the deceased would tell him that she was being harassed for
the demand of dowry.
23. PW11 Dr. Vidit Pande is the doctor, who first saw the
deceased Arti when she was brought to hospital in 108 vehicle.
24. PW12 Mahesh Chandra Tiwari was the medical
technician in the 108 vehicle, when deceased was taken by the 108
vehicle. According to him, he tried to check the pulse of the deceased,
but could not find it. Deceased was serious and when she was taken in
the vehicle, her family members also took along a bucket with little water
in it.
25. PW13 Subhash Chandra Arya is the Secretary in the
Arya Samaj Mandir, Rudrapur. He proved the marriage certificate of
appellant Ravi Pande and deceased Arti and other documents.

11
26. PW14 Bagwati Devi states that a few days before her
death, deceased Arti revealed it to her that dowry is being demanded
from her.
27. PW15 Mahesh Chandra Joshi is the first Investigating
Officer, who prepared the site plan and interrogated the witnesses and
spoken about forensic science laboratory report. PW16 Veer Singh is the
Circle Officer, Bageswar, who finally carried out the investigation and
submitted chargesheet.
28. PW17 Dr. Dayal Sharan is the In-charge of Forensic
Science Laboratory. He has stated about the clothes, bucket, viscera, etc.
and also about organo-chloro insecticide, which was detected in these
articles.
29. DW1 Ruchi Pande states that on the date of incident, her
parents had left the house for the hospital. She had gone to the shop of
her father. On that day, she had left her mobile phone at her house,
therefore, at about 10:00 AM, she suddenly came to her house, there she
saw that the deceased was in a compromising position with the boy. She
immediately informed it to DW2 Ganga Devi and also saw the boy
running out from the house. Thereafter, she went to the shop and
subsequently she was informed that deceased Arti is not well. She came
back and joined PW2 Vimla Devi while they were taking the deceased
Arti to hospital.

12
30. DW2 Ganga Devi is also a relative of the deceased Arti
and the appellants. She has stated about the relationship between the
parties and corroborated the statement of DW1 Ruchi Pande and
deceased Arti having been found in the compromising position.
According to her, relationship of appellants and deceased were very
cordial. In fact, in the last sentence of her examination-in-chief, this
witness states that deceased and Ruchi Pande used to dance in the music.
31. DW3 Jagdish Chandra is the owner of car. According to
him, on 13.09.2017, appellant Mahesh Chandra Pande, Tarkeshwari Devi
hired his car. They took Basanti Devi (mother of the appellant Mahesh
Chandra Pande) to hospital in his car at about 06:00 in the morning.
32. This is a case based on circumstantial evidence.
Undoubtedly, the deceased died within a few months of her marriage.
Admittedly, her husband Ravi Pande, who is the appellant, had left for
job just after 12-13 days of his marriage. Marriage was not solemnized in
the village. Deceased died in the village Manyura. It is also established
from the evidence that a day after the marriage of deceased Arti,
appellants Mahesh Chandra Pande and Tarkeshwari Devi had also left for
Delhi.
33. According to the appellants, Mahesh Chandra Pande and
Tarkeshwari Devi had returned on 12.09.2017, but it is the statement of
defence witness that there is no evidence substantiating these statements.

13
There is no document to this effect, which would have been perhaps
produced. That is one aspect of the matter.
34. There is no dispute about the fact that the deceased Arti
died due to the consumption of poison. Forensic Science Laboratory
report is on the file. In the viscera, empty bucket and plastic bottle
containing 100 ml. water, organo-chloro insecticide poison was detected.
PW2 Vimla Devi's statement requires scrutiny. According to her, she
was called by her niece Monu that deceased Arti had consumed poison
and she was calling her. This statement of PW2 Vimla Devi is recorded
at page two. In the following lines, this witness states that Monu had told
that deceased had been administered poison. The niece Monu has not
been examined. Why? It is not explained by the prosecution. There is
another witness namely Bhagirathi Devi to this effect, who speaks that on
the date of incident, deceased Arti had called her requesting that her
mother be called. This witness proceeded to call Vimla Devi, but on her
way, she found Monali and she conveyed Monali the message of
deceased Arti that her mother may be called. According to it, PW7
Bhagirathi Devi was the first person who saw deceased after she drank
water but deceased did not tell anything to her about the appellant's
conspiring and poisoning the water. She has not stated anything more
than calling her mother. As stated, Monali is not examined.
35. Before statement of Vimla Devi is analyzed further in
this aspect, it would be expedient to examine the delay in lodging FIR.
PW2 Vimla Devi in her statement would speak that 2-3 days after death

14
of her daughter, she lodged FIR. Why FIR was not promptly lodged? On
13.09.2017, deceased Arti died. On that day itself, her inquest and post-mortem was conducted. Next day, she was cremated and next possible
time, PW2 Vimla Devi lodged the report. It would have been a very
sound and convincing explanation, had the Police not intervened at the
time of death of deceased Arti. PW2 states that in the hospital Revenue
Officer had come and he had taken into custody the bucket and water in
it. Prior to it, when deceased was taken to hospital, it is PW11 Dr. Vidit
Pande, who first attended her. According to him, condition of the
deceased Arti was very poor. This witness informed Revenue Officer
PW5 Tribhuwan Singh Bora. The communication by the Doctor is Ex.A-12. According to it, it was told to this witness that the deceased had
consumed poisonous substance. Ex.A-12 does not mention that it was
told to the doctor that the deceased was administered poison instead, as
stated, what is written in it is that the deceased had consumed poison. It
may be seen a little further. It is PW5 Tribhuwan Singh Bora, who
prepared inquest, which is Ex.A-4 on the record. At page 2 of it, it is
recorded that death of deceased occurred due to consumption of poison
(Vispan), not because administration of poison.
36. PW4 Tara Datt Khulbe is one of the witnesses of this
inquest. The question is if PW5 Tribhuwan Singh Bora had reached at the
spot, where the deceased died and he was told about the incident by PW2
Vimla Devi. As stated, why the FIR was not lodged on that day? As
stated, according to the memo sent by PW11 Dr. Vidit Pande to PW5
Tribhuwan Singh Bora (Ex.A-12), the deceased Arti had consumed

15
poison and was admitted in the hospital in a critical state. In the inquest
also, what is recorded is consumption of poison by the deceased.
37. Another question related to it is that if the bucket with
some liquid substance was taken by PW5 Tribhuwan Singh Bora on
13.09.2017 in the hospital, where was it kept by him till 16.09.2017,
when the FIR was lodged? In whose custody was it? When was it given
to the Investigating Officer? Where is the evidence that it was not
tempered with till the time some substance was produced before the
Magistrate and forwarded to the Forensic Science Laboratory. There is
no evidence to this effect. The recovery memo of the bottle of water and
an empty bucket is Ex.A-8, which is proved by PW5 Tribhuwan Singh
Bora. According to this, a bucket filled with water was found near
waiting room and PW2 Vimla Devi had told to PW5 Tribhuwan Singh
Bora that the deceased consumed water from this bucket. What is stated
herein that it was smelling foul, stinking and it was taken for forensic
examination. Water from the bucket was kept in a bottle. In this Ex. A-8
the time, at which this water was taken into custody, has not been
recorded. PW5 Tribhuwan Singh Bora states that he took into custody red
coloured plastic bucket which was empty and a plastic bottle filled with
water. (Page 3, Para 2) There is contradiction in the recovery memo.
According to Ex.A-8, PW5 Tribhuwan Singh Bora took into custody
bucket which was filled with water and this water was kept in a bottle for
forensic examination. What PW5 Tribhuwan Singh Bora took into
custody a bucket filled with water, by taking sample of water in a bottle,
as recorded in the recovery memo or an empty bucket and a bottle of

16
water, as stated by him in the court. This is major contradiction. If PW5
Tribhuwan Singh Bora took empty bucket and a bottle of water into
custody then there are many other questions as to who took the water in
the bottle? From where the water was kept in the bottle? In whose
presence, it was done? It further makes prosecution case doubtful.
38. What is important is that according to recovery memo,
Ex. A-8, this water in the bucket was smelling foul. It was stinking. Now,
the question is if it was so stinking that even PW5 Tribhuwan Singh Bora
could smell it in the hospital, how could the deceased drink the water
without realizing that it is smelling foul and stinking. She would also had
smelled that the water is stinking. It doubts the prosecution case. Delayed
FIR under those circumstances makes the FIR as well as the entire
prosecution case doubtful.
39. Arguments have been advanced with regard to section
106 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. It is true that if a fact is within the
especial knowledge of the accused, section 106 of the Indian Evidence
Act, 1872 requires that such fact must be proved by the accused.
40. According to learned State Counsel, deceased died in the
house of the appellant. It is not a case in which provision of section 106
of the Indian Evidence Act could be invoked. For the simple reason that
the cause of the death is known. Her death is due to poison. The only
question is whether the appellants administered her poison or she
otherwise consumed the poison. It is not a case within the especial

17
knowledge of the appellants. PW2 Vimla Devi herself has stated that
according to deceased, none of the family members were in the house.
What is most interesting to notice is that appellant Ravi Pande was not in
the village. He was in the Army. How could he be connected with the
mixing of poison with the water? How could deceased drink such a
water, which is so stinking and foul without realizing that there was
something wrong with the water? Argument has also been advanced with
regard to applicability of Section 6 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
Undoubtedly, the principle of res gestae makes such statement relevant,
but here deceased had not seen anyone mixing the poison in the water.
According to the prosecution, she drank water without realizing that it is
stinking and foul. It is also doubtful. Therefore, her statement is relevant
to the extent that she had consumed poisonous substance, but, it cannot
be stretched to the level that appellants mixed poison in the water.
41. Prosecution tried to prove that soon before her death, the
deceased was harassed for the demand of dowry. PW6 Neema Khulbe
has stated that the deceased Arti told it to her that the appellant Ravi
Pande had stopped talking to her for about 15 days prior to her death. But
this statement of PW6 Neema Khulbe gets falsified by the statement of
PW16 Veer Singh, the Investigating Officer. PW16 Veer Singh (page 3
of the statement) has stated that both appellants Ravi Pandey and
deceased Arti were talking to each other over their mobile phones till
13.09.2017. But, according to PW16 Veer Singh, there was no telephone
call between PW6 Neema Khulbe and deceased Arti in the months of
September, 2017.

18
42. FIR is delayed in the case. The explanation is not
reasonable for it. Statement of PW2 Vimla Devi is not inspiring
confidence; it is doubtful as to what was taken into custody by PW5
Tribhuwan Singh Bora on 13.09.2017? Bucket with water or empty
bucket and water in a bottle? Where did PW5 Tribhuwan Singh Bora
kept the bucket till 16.09.2017, when the FIR was lodged? According to
PW11 Dr. Vidit Pandey, who first attended the deceased Arti, was told
that the deceased consumed poison. In the inquest also, it is recorded that
the deceased Arti consumed poison; in both these documents, it is not
recorded that the deceased was administered poison or by accident, the
deceased took poison; if the liquid in the bucket was stinking in the
hospital as told by PW5 Tribhuwan Singh Bora, how deceased Arti drank
such water with foul smell without realizing that there is something
wrong with the water? Investigating Officerr stated that deceased Arti
and appellant Ravi Pande were talking to each other till 13.09.2017;
appellants were not at home when the incident occurred. Having
considered this and all the other relevant factors, this Court is of the view
that the prosecution failed to prove the charges against the appellants and
appellants deserved to be acquitted of the charges under sections 302,
498-A IPC. Accordingly, appeal deserves to be allowed.
43. The appeal is allowed. Impugned judgment and order
dated 01.10.2018, in so far as, it convicts the appellants, is set aside.
Appellants are acquitted of the charges under sections 302 and 498-A
also.

19
44. Appellants are on bail. Appellants shall furnish personal
bonds and two sureties by each one of them, each of the like amount, to
the satisfaction of the court concerned, under section 437-A of the Code.
45. Let a copy of the judgment along with lower court record be
sent to the court below for compliance.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.) (Alok Singh, J.)
 07.11.2019
Ujjwal
